en.name: Rye flour
en.summary: Rye flour keeps 3 months in the pantry and 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). As with every flour milled with the germ in, it is the oil going rancid rather than anything microbial that ends a bag.
en.pantry: 3 months in an airtight container on a cool, dark, dry shelf. Rye flour is usually sold with some or all of the bran and germ still in it — that is what gives rye bread its depth — and that means oil in the flour and a shorter life than white wheat flour. Rye also carries more pentosans, which attract moisture, so a bag in a humid kitchen clumps before it goes rancid. Fresh rye flour smells faintly sweet and earthy; stale rye smells sharp, and the bitterness carries straight into the loaf.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for rye flour. The fridge slows the oil and is a reasonable option for a bag you will work through over a season, but the container must be genuinely airtight — rye flour is unusually good at taking up moisture, and a cold bag opened in a warm kitchen condenses water straight into it. If you also keep a rye starter, note that the starter is a live culture with entirely different rules and does not belong in this record.
en.freezer: 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F), the sensible default for more flour than a season's baking. Use an airtight tub or a double bag with the air pressed out, and label it clearly. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that window; what runs out is flavour as the oil slowly oxidises. Bring the sealed container up to room temperature before opening, and let the flour reach room temperature before you mix a dough — cold rye flour hydrates unevenly and a rye dough is sticky enough already.
en.thawing: Let the sealed container warm to room temperature before opening so the flour does not take up condensation. Give the flour itself time to warm before mixing a dough.
spoilage: A sharp, oily or paint-like smell — rancid germ oil.
A bitter aftertaste in bread made to a recipe that used to work.
Hard clumps or a caked surface, which means moisture reached the flour.
Webbing, larvae or small moths in the bag.
tips: Decant into an opaque airtight tub as soon as you open the bag.
Buy the amount you will bake through in a season.
Smell before you bake; rancidity arrives before the date does.
Freeze a new bag hard for a couple of days to kill any weevil eggs.

faq.q: How long does rye flour last?
faq.a: 3 months in an airtight container in the pantry, or 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Seal it airtight and let it come back to room temperature before opening, and before mixing a dough.

faq.q: Why does my rye flour clump?
faq.a: Rye is high in pentosans, which attract moisture. In a humid kitchen it cakes well before it goes rancid, so keep it properly sealed.

zh.name: 黑麥粉
zh.summary: 黑麥粉密封放常溫可放 3 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 6 個月。和所有帶胚芽磨的粉一樣，終結一袋粉的是油脂油耗，而不是任何微生物。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐、放陰涼避光乾燥的架子，3 個月。黑麥粉通常保留部分或全部的麩皮與胚芽——那正是黑麥麵包風味厚實的來源——也因此粉裡帶油，壽命比白麵粉短。黑麥的戊聚醣含量也高，很會抓水，所以在潮濕的廚房裡，它往往先結塊、再油耗。新鮮黑麥粉聞起來微甜、帶土壤感；走味的則刺鼻，而那股苦會直接跑進麵包裡。
zh.fridge: 黑麥粉沒有公布的冷藏期限。冷藏能拖慢油脂，對一季內用得完的份量是合理的做法，但容器必須真正密封——黑麥粉特別會吸濕，一包冰過的粉在溫暖廚房裡打開，水氣會直接凝進去。另外提醒：如果你同時養黑麥酸種，那是活的菌種，規則完全不同，不屬於這一篇。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 6 個月；超過一季用量的話，這就是合理的預設。用密封罐或套兩層袋、壓出空氣，並清楚標示。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；先用完的是風味，因為油脂仍在慢慢氧化。開蓋前先讓整罐回到室溫；調麵團前也要讓粉本身回到室溫——冰冷的黑麥粉吸水不均，而黑麥麵團本來就夠黏了。
zh.thawing: 整罐密封著回到室溫再開蓋，粉才不會受潮。調麵團前也給粉一點回溫的時間。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、帶油味或油漆味——胚芽油耗了。
用一向沒問題的配方做出來的麵包卻有苦的餘韻。
結成硬塊或表面結成一層餅，表示水氣碰到粉了。
袋子裡出現絲網、幼蟲或小蛾。
tips: 拆封後立刻倒進不透光的密封罐。
買一季內烤得完的份量。
烤之前先聞；油耗比日期更早現形。
新買的整袋先冷凍凍硬兩三天，把蟲卵殺掉。

faq.a: 密封放常溫 3 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 6 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 6 個月。密封好，開蓋前和調麵團前都先讓它回到室溫。
黑麥的戊聚醣含量高、很會抓水。在潮濕的廚房裡它往往先結塊、才油耗，所以要確實密封。
